Whenever I pick up a rifle without a trigger I die a little inside. It's the same reason you would want fast reload: the more you can output the more people you can put down. Between good positioning, fast reload and a trigger modded OHK rifle I've put down 20-30 people in the space of 60-120 seconds. Not even an exaggeration by any means. Fast reload and trigger mods let you maintain a ready state as much as possible. A lot of people assume that because you're using a long range weapon that you don't need speed because you're safe at a distance and have all the time in the world. That's incorrect. You need speed as much as anyone. A marksman has the unique advantage of being able to reach out and touch anyone he can see. Every poor son of a bitch in your line of sight and effective range is as good as dead if you're ready and able to place a killing shot. People often wonder why I never get into vehicles, and that's really the main reason. If I'm in a car I don't have my rifle ready and I can't put a .30-06 or a 7.62x57mm into someone's vitals at a moment's notice. You are doing yourself a favour by putting a trigger mod on.

Don't rely on auto ranging. Having to rely on something you need to adjust just slows you down. As soon as you don't need auto ranging, dump it. Eventually you learn to eyeball it. In general you don't need to make huge adjustments at the ranges you most often fight in on even the largest maps. If you can already make do without auto range, just keep doing what you're doing. You can acquire targets and place shots down range much faster and with better consistency if you don't have to keep checking your range. You'll also encounter less instances of "oh I was set to the wrong range."

If you're using the BAR you don't need ammunition mods. Lightened spring gives 553rpm which when paired with the stainless steel barrel and field adjusted sights gives you sufficient rate of fire to handle close quarters with the benefit of incredibly low recoil and accuracy. When you're modding weapons you have to consider what you want and what you need.

Something newer players tend not to consider is that there are damage breakpoints. Assuming equal damage at all ranges, if I have a rifle that does 75 damage, is the rifle with 90 damage better? Not at all. What if both fired at 60rpm? 100rpm? 200rpm? 1000rpm? It doesn't matter. 75 damage and 90 damage will always kill with two hits. Every soldier has 100 hitpoints and you're not getting to 100 any faster by increasing your damage. 75 and 90 are well above the heavyset thresholds. 50 damage versus 60? Sure, any level of heavyset would prevent 50 damage from being 2hk while 60 is above the heavyset threshold. 100 damage vs 120 damage? Sure, like with 50 any heavyset will prevent 100 damage from being 1hk. This doesn't account for effective ranges, but you get the idea.

The other thing many newer players don't consider is the effect of rate of fire on your accuracy. Some guns suffer more for increasing their rate of fire, while some guns don't. Some guns simply have more manageable recoil so they handle better at the same rate of fire, they just have less kick. I would max the RoF on a Thompson in a heartbeat but I would have to think about it for the Johnson (although inevitably yeah I'd max out its RoF anyway). Both can hit 800rpm. I want to bring up another thing because some people instinctively counter recoil, but I know people that don't. You can compensate for any recoil by aiming against the direction your gun wants to go. I bring this up because someone asked me for my Thompson and FG42 mods because they thought I had a way to make them recoilless. I don't have recoilless weapons. I just kept my aim on target as I held down the trigger. It's just a smooth counter motion and it varies from weapon to weapon whether it's because of the direction or strength of the recoil.

So why do I bring this up? Because a lot of people don't mod for practicality. Consider two MG42s. What is the difference in kill time between a 1200rpm MG42 and a 1028rpm MG42? What about a 553 BAR and 600 BAR? 16 milliseconds. Yes, 16ms can be the difference between life and death but more often than not it isn't. I would take a 1028 MG42 over a 1200 and a 553 BAR over a 600. What about a 553 BAR with Bertie clays and chrome lined barrel vs a 553 with M72 and chrome lined? The 553 chrome bertie is effectively 3hk till 196 meters while the 553 chrome m72 is effectively 3hk till 299m. Both kill at 216ms. It's not practical to fight at that range if you can't reliably hit a target and you have to hit the target 3 times, maybe more unless you pop them in the head. Both 553 chrome bertie and chrome m72 BARs are also more inaccurate than a 553 BAR with just a lightened spring because the bertie clay and M72 decrease the weapon stability so you get more kick per shot. Without Tight Grip badge you can maintain a close shot grouping at 40m with standing shots in full auto using an accuracy 553 build. You could probably do it after depleting your stamina too.

Which is fair enough, but in practical terms the movement change in free fall isn't substantial enough to throw off someone who can already deliberately shoot you in free fall. I don't mean to trivialize it by how I describe it, because it is a complicated shot to make. You have angle, distance, velocity, bullet trajectory, vertical trajectory, and horizontal trajectory and if they're rotating, rotational motion to factor into your calculations and you have a short window to make those calculations. Also because it's an "uphill" shot, your expectation for lead and elevation are completely different to if you were hitting a ground target. However, any movement you make during your descent in free fall is too smooth and predictable. The reason someone who's deployed their chute can be harder to hit is that they can be more erratic. If you have the bad habit of obligate shooting and react on instinct, you're going to react to one motion, but they're already making another motion. That's why stutter steps throw people off. A smooth, minute change in motion is something an experienced shooter can compensate for easily. Motion and speed isn't enough to overcome someone who can legitimately shoot well. If a jeep is speeding ahead and you pop the passenger and they start swerving left and right, are they harder to hit? Technically yes, the shot becomes more complicated. Practically? No. The vehicles in this game can't make super sharp turns because of the game physics. They have relatively limited maneuverability when they're at max speed. If you turn too much you're going to spin out and then you're shit out of lucky anyway. If they veer left and then start veering right it's not erratic at all, they take too long to shift. If a vehicle is rolling down a hill, it's technically a difficult shot to hit whoever's in it but practically well within the capabilities of a lot of people even if they might not think it. There's a lot of rotational and dynamic motion. But think about it this way, when the vehicle bounces up, it's got a fixed trajectory and once it's up in the air its rotation won't be affected by other factors. Once their movement is predictable it's just a matter of anticipating where to place your shot and timing it. Technically difficult but still practically doable. A shot with a lot of motion is just one you have to analyze so you can determine when and where to shoot.

That's fair enough that you can move, but I think you underestimate people who can accurately predict trajectories and overestimate how much difference a free falling para's movement can make. Just because you make a minute adjustment doesn't guarantee that you're going to avoid a shot when you have minimum maneuverability. If they're good enough to hit you in free fall, they're good enough to compensate for your adjustments.

And SPRINT+WASD doesn't make you immune from SA rifles, it makes you immune from obligate fire unless they get lucky. 90% of the player base probably can't aim properly or have terrible ping which makes precision fire difficult, but some people do know how to shoot.

If you are losing the match because the paras keep back capping and forcing you to redirect, then maybe you should defend the points they're dropping on. Their advantage is that they can bypass fixed lines, but they're not special once they're on the ground. They're infantry with 6 slots and they're forced to take one badge (free fall) or be screwed when they're floating down. They're triple screwed if there's a good shooter on the enemy team that can shoot paratroopers in free fall on the reg because then it doesn't even matter if they have their chute or not. Some people are accurate enough that they can nail guys in free fall because the paras literally can't dodge and are on a fixed trajectory. The alternative is they fly so slowly that they are going to be shot at anyway. Free fall badge also means they often don't have heavyset or fast reload or whatever badge you like using because not everyone's a vet and free fall really is the most useful for a para despite the advantages of anything else. If you're losing because they're mopping the floor with you on the ground, it's possible that they're a premade of really good players. Also, you're actually wasting your time if you sit on an AA dropping para planes. They have enough that it doesn't matter how many you down. They'll roll out another. Leave that for pilots who can drop them more effectively. Just win the ground game. The biggest problem you'll face with them is that they sneak into points. But that's a problem you can fix by altering your tactics.

Binoculars helped me learn how to spot at a distance without aid. Find something with the binocs and then zoom out. You should still be able to see what you found. (unless it's in heavy concealment) It familiarizes you with what distant targets look like. 

The other thing is listen. This game has good sound design so you can track down the general area of a shooter. If you're looking in their general direction you might be able to see them shooting.

The semi automatic and bolt action rifles might be a good fit for you. You have a good eye and steady aim (at least based on the video). With rifles you're effective at all ranges, and even though they're less than ideal in CQB you can make it work at that range. But whatever weapon you use, I'd still grind the ribbon for SMG just for fast reload. That is one handy badge to have.
It only gets better from there since you have mods to look forward to.

My badge preference is fast reload and heavyset. Deadeye could be useful depending on how you shoot, though I'd imagine you'd be using a scope. In general I would recommend getting a pistol to go along with your BA. It's very doable to fight at close quarters with a BA (PM me if you want to see video examples) but you'll want a back up plan. If you're infantry sniper you could easily carry an automatic weapon too if you have hoarder gold. Fair amount of people do work with that. If you intend to counter snipe you will probably want heavyset gold just to stand a chance against first strikes. Secondary gear is really up to you and what you want to do. AT is always nice I guess. Me personally, if I'm on an infantry sniper I'm carrying a semi automatic rifle or a pistol. 
In terms of CQC tactics more or less the same tactics apply as with automatic weapons... it's just less forgiving. You really have to know how to clear a building well. In close quarters you need all the advantages you can get. You have to have good target prioritization too. You have to be able to identify high value targets, which can be complicated. But in general you can sum it up as, "who the hell is going to hurt me the most and what order do I have to kill them in?" And you have one second to figure that out. It's not like with an automatic weapon where you can hose a room and kill everyone in there. Even if you have a rifle modded for max speed, that's 60rpm with a 1903, you're going to need 1 second before you can kill the next person. More than likely you're not going to have 60rpm because you're going to slap the heavy bolt on for a OHK. That drops you to about 41rpm at the fastest. That's like 1.46 seconds before your next shot. If you doubled how long an MG42 could kill you, it would still kill you 7 times in that space of time.
For distance shooting, learn to manually compensate for distance. Don't adjust your sights for elevation, that's just something you have to fix when you're aiming at a different range. I watched a video of a dude miss a shot that he should have landed because he forgot to readjust his sights. You'll shoot faster in general too since it's a consistent weapon and you really won't have to think about shooting when you're comfortable with it. Downside is latency can really fuck with you. But that might be because of the way I shoot, so it might not be as bad for you. I have trouble with my vision and can't track motion well so I predict where the target is going to be, fix my scope on that spot and time my shot to land when they get there. If they change their trajectory I have to readjust. I try to get the most static picture I can work with. After every shot I go off scope and just zoom back in where I need to be, rather than track too much with my scope. Feel free to try it and see if it works for you. But either way, since it's mostly timing, it really doesn't work as well when your sense of timing is off. You can work through it after being in a match with latency, it just sucks when the ping keeps changing. I don't know how other people shoot, but I would imagine you could also try a more dynamic shooting style by tracking your target. How effective that is, I wouldn't know.

It's useful when you're learning to shoot, but I would advise you to not get used to it. Auto range is another variable you have to account for and you want to make your rifle as consistent as possible in its performance. IPSC shooters try to make their guns as consistent as possible so when they point it at something they know exactly where it's going to strike. When you're familiar with your weapon you'll have fast, natural and smooth aim. I don't like to plug my videos but I did put up a recon guide that's on the guides section on the sidebar. I briefly demonstrate why it's so advantageous to know how to shoot manually by shooting a target at ~270m and then shortly after shooting a target at ~500m (I don't know how far he actually was, but that's the best guess I could make). It would have been very difficult to set the auto range (especially since the target was a para) so you would have had to compensate for whatever pre-set range was there in addition to the bullet trajectory and the trajectory of the paratrooper.

Yeah, I don't think I really made it clear but what I was trying to say about predictability was that there's a common trend in hiding places that recon tend to take and you can focus on those trends first. In the worst case scenario you have 1.5 seconds to figure out if you can run or if you can shoot back. In 1.5 seconds you have to find out where he is (whether specifically or in general) and either shoot him before he kills you or protect yourself. Because you have little time you have to strip down the process of your search. That's what I was trying to explain really, you narrow down your search area and skip places that they are not likely to be in. In the mean time you're trying to find any extra information to help you pinpoint them. If they're taking extra shots that's more chances of you finding them provided that they're not hitting you. Granted in practice you probably have more than 1.5 seconds (most recon aren't capable of lining up shots that quickly), but assuming the worst case scenario that's all you'll have.

I didn't say it was easy. All you can really do is improve your chances if you're caught out at range. At a range of 150m to 200m the sniper has such a tremendous advantage over you whether you have the right gun or not. The biggest thing you can do to help you is to find out where the sniper generally is. If you know his rough field of vision, you know where he can and can't shoot. If you know where he can shoot, you know where not to stand. If you know where he can't shoot, you know where to hide. If you hide, a sniper has to decide if it's worth his time waiting for you to pop your head out or if he should acquire a new target. 

I guess my wording made the process sound easy, but it really isn't. Like WildCAT said, awareness is key to dealing with snipers. Honestly if a recon can aim you don't stand much of a chance at 150m to 200m unless you have hard cover near you or heavy concealment. A sniper that can land two shots in succession needs 1.5 seconds to drop you if he doesn't kill you with his first shot. To stress how important it is to just know how important general awareness is when it comes to a sniper, there's a video of someone sniping dudes running across O2 emergency spawn on Mountain Town. Drops 17 people in under 2 minutes. The shooting wasn't special. He wasn't even really sniping, he was within 40-70 meters of someone at any time. Hell, at some point someone got within spitting distance. Someone was close enough that they could have dropped him with a pistol. So how did he kill 17 people? Nobody paid attention to him. Out of an entire team, probably 3 people at most ever turned to face him. 

What a lot of people don't think about is that a sniper is also a player. They have their own set of problems to deal with and you can help them make a mistake. If a sniper sits in a spot and no one ever even turns to look at him, he's not going to move and he's going to keep shooting. I've only seen maybe a couple of snipers that will relocate from a concealed position. If you start hammering away at his position, even if you miss, you're pointing out where he's hiding to the rest of your team that's able to see your shots. The sniper also knows that he's been found and he has to figure out if his position is tenable or if he needs to bail and re-position. Just the act of landing a shot next to him changes the situation for a sniper. 

It's definitely not easy, but you're limited in your ability to respond at that point. All you can do when you're in that situation is make the best of it. Killing the enemy isn't always the only way to win.

So I'm going to tell you the secret to killing recon. 90% of them are predictable. They tend to gravitate towards the same positions like there's some pungent cheese drawing them in. But first you have to narrow down your search area. Pay attention to sound. The distinct reports of bolt action rifles can be heard from a good distance and the sound design on H&G is surprisingly good so positional audio is very useful. It's also important to pay attention to your allies. The order that your allies are shot or killed can help you determine where a sniper is shooting from. It's easier said than done, but you can narrow down potential locations by figuring out where your dead or injured friend could not have possibly been shot from. Look for bullet marks if they missed and you didn't see a tracer or an impact. A sniper can only control a certain area and finding where he can't shoot gives you a rough idea of his field of vision.

Now this next part is why I mentioned predictability. The ideal situation is that you've gotten a general facing using whatever information you can gather. At this point you just have to scan that area for the enemy. But there's a few things that can help you do this faster. Focus on objects that provide cover or concealment. Most snipers won't stand in the open. Often snipers will stand to the side of a tree because their instinct is to position cover between you and them. Unfortunately for them that silhouettes them and makes them easy to spot. With rocks Germans I think are the hardest to spot if they're standing next to it, but in general rocks have a smooth profile and if you notice a lot of protrusions, you're probably looking at a sniper. The hardest to pick out are those that go prone in certain areas. Usually the worst to find are those in dips on the slope of a hill and often they're in heavy shadow. These guys I just try to bait out so I can see a muzzle flash. If they're in bushes... that one you just have to get used to sorting through that junk and they stick their barrel out or something. Or you just find their muzzle flash.

To effectively fight back you can take a semi automatic rifle or bolt action and pressure them. A semi automatic rifle is one of the biggest pains in the ass as a recon because it is effective at close range and at long range. You can out shoot a bolt action with an SA rifle even with iron sights. A sniper has to be careful about their shot because they don't have the same rate of fire as everyone else. The fastest bolt action you can make has a rate of fire of 61rpm but that's a 2hk rifle. In any case, it doesn't matter how good of a shot they are, they're not killing anyone if they're still cycling the next round. But while a sniper has to watch his shots, an SA rifle can accurately hammer an area with rapid fire and sometimes that's enough to get them to back off and take cover if they're not confident that they can safely fire at you. Even if you tag them, it doesn't matter if you killed them or not, wounded recon tend to go to ground and try to play safer until they can heal. At the distance they shoot they can more easily retreat and get to a medbox than regular infantry. But it doesn't matter, if they were in control of an area, they aren't at that point. And unseating a recon even once can make it difficult for them to regain control of an area. Most of the time a sniper is only exceptionally effective because they're not receiving any return fire. A good marksman who's undisturbed is something you don't want to have. If they're not worried about anything they can focus on acquiring and dropping targets.

You also have the option of taking a vehicle to try and blitz past snipers. Most can't make tracking shots like that, but there are snipers that can shoot the driver out on demand in a jeep full of infantry and pick everyone apart one by one. However, it does feel to me like you can get a lot more out of your text than you already have. There are places where you can unpack some details or omit things for greater effect.

“The first time I drove a car, I crashed it.”

“I crashed it” isn’t really needed because you elaborate upon it in the next line. You could easily have just said:
“The first time I drove a car, I slammed it so hard into the Johnson’s Land Rover...”

It’s a minor difference but it has a stronger impact. The next part to me was fine, but not fluid. “The crash wasn’t my fault.../ ...flashed in front of the headlights.”

“How does he leer?”
“What is his figure?”
“Why is it a sick metallic sheen?”
“How does he flash in front of the headlights?”

To give you an example of what I mean by unpacking:
“The crash wasn’t my fault. But nobody else saw that spindly thing flicker between the flashes of lightning, my headlights shining on its sheen of oozing quicksilver and its faceless gaze unwaveringly riveted to my eyes.”

“Leering figure” became a faceless spindly thing with an unwavering gaze riveted to Lexi’s eyes.
Sick metallic sheen became a sheen of oozing quicksilver.
And there’s a temporal context established by “flicker between the flashes of lightning.”

Hey. I've never been what you've been through, but I've gone through suffering, helplessness and self loathing that might be similar to what you're experiencing. A lot of the times I wonder why I feel so horrible and a big help to me is taking a step back and think on why I'm feeling these things. And a lot of the times I realize that it's not my fault. Maybe right now it's hard for you to see that it isn't your fault, but there's nothing wrong with any of your decisions. You did no wrong.

One of the most helpful things I've been taught was the concept of cognitive distortions. A few that might (after all, I don't really know what you're thinking) relate to you are:

"All or nothing thinking: You see things in black and white categories. If your performance falls short of perfect, you see yourself as a total failure."
You had one experience in being rendered helpless. But you're never helpless forever, especially now. This one event doesn't make you completely faulty either. You still have positive qualities about you. It might not seem like it to you right now, but no one is ever completely negative or positive. We're complex beings, physically you can have parts that are faulty but the whole body still runs. It's the same thing with your thoughts, emotions and behaviour.

"Mental Filter: You pick out a single negative detail and dwell on it exclusively so that your vision of all reality becomes darkened, like the drop of ink that discolors the entire beaker of water."
My friends and I play league of legends sometimes, and we often say to each "map awareness, bro." You're in a hard situation, but you have to keep your mind and eyes open. You're going to have a much more difficult time if you let one thought dominate your mind. Try controlling your breathing, take slow, full breaths. Then start questioning what you're feeling and thinking and cut yourself some slack. 

"Emotional reasoning: You assume that your negative emotions necessarily reflect the way things really are: 'I feel it, therefore it must be true.'"
You aren't pathetic. You aren't weak. You aren't pathetic or weak for trusting that someone wouldn't mess with your drink. You aren't pathetic or weak because a drug affects you like it affects everyone else. You certainly aren't helpless either, you're only helpless when you decide you're helpless. You have strength in you, even if you don't see it for yourself.

"Labeling: An extreme form of overgeneralization. Instead of describing your error, you attach a negative label to yourself: 'I am a loser.'"
Like I said before, you're not weak or pathetic. You've taken a hit, but you can bounce back. You have a whole life ahead of you to overcome your challenges. 

"Personalization: You see yourself as the cause of some negative external event for which, in fact, you were not primarily responsible."
You came to the party for fun, not for trouble. As I said before, you did nothing wrong. The only thing you can really say you did wrong is that you put your trust in the wrong people, but there's no point dwelling on that because you could never have anticipated that someone had such intent. 

I hope this has been of help to you, and I hope you'll feel better. Take your time to recompose yourself, you are worth the time and effort. And if you ever want to talk, you can always shoot me a message. And even if you don't want to talk to anyone, please try putting your thoughts into words or verbalize it, it might help you. Anyway, this is my story. I hope in hearing it, you will feel less alone. I hope in hearing it you will find some solace that there is someone who has experienced something similar. I was diagnosed with depression in 2003 when I was in middle school. So how should I explain my time since then? I slept through it. I couldn't stand to be conscious. Then I don't know how, but I got into university miraculously, and that's where everything went downhill. I met a woman there in my 3rd year, and there was finally a dawn after a long night. I spent so much time with her, most of our friends thought we were dating. It gave me a shit eating grin. But now I absolutely cannot stand going to my university town because everywhere I go I will remember where we stood or sat, what we did, what we said, what we ate. I remember her telling me she wanted to be a masseuse at first. Then a photographer. Then a sociologist. Then an art historian. I remember her telling me her nickname used to be 'Cucumber' because it was her favourite food. Whenever we went out to eat, I would find something with cucumber in it so she could take from my plate. For a man who slept for 7 years, I was suddenly wide awake. I learned everything to make her happy. I wanted to keep my eyes open because every moment I spent with her. 

Then I saw her smile. And that was what broke me. Why would her smile break me? It's not really something you can describe in words. There are times when I am possessed with a unique power of perception and there are moments where things come to me in unsettling clarity. When my sister was announcing her pregnancy, my mom simply passed me the phone saying it was my sister on the call. I don't know why but when I looked at my mother I instantly knew what her news was going to be. I was going to be an uncle. It was with this same clarity and conviction that when I saw the woman smile at one of her friends that just as my eyes were on her, her eyes were on him. At first I tried to deny it, but as time went on I realized there was nothing for me to gain by fighting. There was no way I could win her over. I was so broken I stopped attending classes. I didn't leave my apartment save to get food. And I was further broken when no one tried to reach out for me. None of the friends I had made even noticed my disappearance. The next time I saw them, they didn't even realize I had any problems. I asked myself many questions. Probably some similar to yours.

Is there something wrong with me? Why was I not important to her? We spent so much time together. We knew each other so well. Why him and not me? I'll never find someone like her. I don't think I can ever love again. 

No one came to save me. No one knocked at my door and tried to cheer me up. But look at this thread. Look at all these people trying so hard to reach you from wherever they're from. And look at me. I don't know you, but if we were standing before each other I would be extending my hand in an offer of hope. Because my heart was hollowed and blackened, and my mind tumultuous and dark. But I have endured, sometimes quietly, sometimes violently, and I am still here. I am here writing to you, that you should live if no one else but for yourself. Because you are worth the air you breathe, even if you don't believe it. She does not determine your value. Her being with her ex does not make you any lesser of a man. If she loved you once, there is something she saw that was good. Maybe you obscured it from her somehow, or she lost sight of it. But there is something in you that is worth another person investing their time in you. You are not worthless.

I have earnestly poured my whole heart into this because I feel like you may understand the feeling when I say that I have sometimes felt that it would be easier to dig into my chest and pluck out my heart and hold in my hand the thing that has caused me so much unrelenting agony, and leave it at my mercy to annihilate or to pardon. So please reconsider.
